items.excerpt: ## Trump Blasts ICC, Praises Presidents Xi and Putin at Unprecedented Trilateral Summit Nov 19, 2026 The leaders of Russia, China and the United States — Presidents Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump — have wrapped up an unprecedented trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China, with what Chinese media is calling a landmark “peace declaration.” The four-point plan calls for the three nations to reduce nuclear risks, increase oil refining, promote reforms to the United Nations and limit the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court. This is President Trump. > President Donald Trump: “In another area of potential cooperation between us, I’ll be suggesting ways to protect our nation’s sovereignty from rogue globalist organizations such as the International Criminal Court, which has gotten out of control, which I believe we all agree has really strayed far from beyond its jurisdiction.” President Putin faces an ICC warrant seeking his arrest for war crimes committed in Ukraine, including the unlawful transfer of children from Russian-occupied areas. Neither the U.S., nor China, nor Russia is a party to the Rome Statute that established the International Criminal Court. During the summit, President Trump lavished praise on President Xi and referred to President Putin as “my friend.” That prompted Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk to write on social media, “God, protect us from such friends.” ## Democrats Nominate Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker as Progressives Dissent on Healthcare, Gaza and ICE Nov 19, 2026 On Capitol Hill, House Democrats voted 251-11 on Wednesday to nominate New York Congressmember Hakeem Jeffries to be the next speaker of the House. Jeffries is poised to make history as the first African American to fill the role. The vote came during a closed-door caucus meeting. Afterward, seven incoming Democratic congressmembers issued a joint statement explaining their opposition to Jeffries. They wrote, “Whether on Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics, or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate on these issues.” ## Israeli Tanks and Bulldozers Push Past Gaza’s “Yellow Line,” Further Displacing Palestinians Nov 19, 2026 In Gaza, thousands of Palestinians have been forced to flee again after Israeli tanks and bulldozers pushed past the ceasefire’s “Yellow Line” on Wednesday and into Palestinian-held territory. Israeli troops operating east of the “Yellow Line” have gradually pushed the boundary westward and now occupy about two-thirds of Gaza’s territory, with 2 million Palestinians trapped in an increasingly narrow strip of land, most of them forced to live in tents. This is Salam Aql, a Palestinian woman who says she was displaced for the 15th time on Wednesday. ... Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said the military is ready to take more land and turn the newly seized areas into permanent parts of Israel’s security zones. The Palestinian Health Ministry says Israeli forces have killed over 1,600 Palestinians in Gaza since last October’s so-called ceasefire. ... ## World Court Finds Burma Committed Genocide Against Rohingya in 2017 Nov 19, 2026 Judges at the International Court of Justice have found that Burmese security forces committed genocide against Rohingya Muslims during military operations nearly a decade ago. It’s the first time the court has held a nation accountable for violating the 1948 Genocide Convention. The ruling follows the 2017 military crackdown by government forces and ethnic Rakhine mobs that killed about 10,000 people and drove more than 730,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh. ... ## Venezuela Restores Military Ties with U.S., Months After Abduction of President Maduro Nov 19, 2026 Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made a surprise visit to Caracas on Wednesday, where he announced the U.S. and Venezuela have signed an agreement to restore military ties. Under the deal, the two countries will work together on areas such as joint training, intelligence sharing and border security. It’s Hegseth’s first visit to Venezuela since U.S. forces violently abducted former President Nicolás Maduro and his wife, National Assembly deputy Cilia Flores, back in January. The deal comes after months in which Washington has effectively controlled Venezuela’s oil sales.

items.title: Higher fuel prices seep into core inflation - Dallasfed.org
items.excerpt: November 19, 2026 Fuel prices have been on a wild ride since late February 2026, when military strikes on Iran set off sharp moves in oil and fuel markets. Retail gasoline prices aside, the U.S. retail diesel price reached an all-time high, the jet fuel price is near its previous peak, and the heating oil price has set a new record. The U.S. price of natural gas, meanwhile, has barely budged. The fuel price surge has been very uneven. Diesel prices in particular moved sharply higher. Diesel is the fuel of the freight economy. Trucks, trains, ships and farm equipment run on it, which means its price may potentially touch the cost of moving nearly everything consumers buy. The price gap between diesel and gasoline has widened significantly in recent months. On Sept. 22, 2026, the national average retail price of diesel reached $6.53 per gallon, about 70 percent above its level at the end of February (compared with a 50 percent rise for retail gasoline). The diesel rise surpassed the fuel’s previous record set in 2022 (Chart 1). Prices have eased only modestly, to about $6.31 as of the end of October. Consumers experience these prices directly at the pump and indirectly on their utility bills. But fuel prices may also work their way into the prices of other goods and services, from airline tickets to paper towels. Economists call these "second-round effects," and they matter for the Federal Reserve because they show up in core inflation, an inflation measure that excludes food and energy. Policymakers watch core inflation closely to gauge underlying price pressures. Our estimates suggest that higher fuel prices added between 20 and 60 basis points to 12-month core inflation, as measured by the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, as of September 2026. If fuel prices simply held at their current levels, that contribution would gradually decline by about 30 basis points by the end of 2027. ... By construction, core PCE inflation excludes energy. But excluding energy prices from the index doesn't insulate it from their effects. When fuel costs rise, airlines tend to charge more for tickets, shippers tend to raise freight rates and manufacturers that rely on energy-intensive inputs seek to pass along higher costs. The size of these second-round effects is not clear a priori because not all producers can pass on fuel price increases. For example, farmers may find it challenging to pass on higher diesel costs when faced with large corporations buying their crops. ... All of our estimates point to the same conclusion: The pass-through of fuel prices to core PCE inflation is generally small and difficult to estimate precisely, but because this year's fuel price swings have been so large, their second-round effects on core inflation are not negligible.

items.title: AI surge could strain US capacity and overheat economy, Fed’s Goolsbee says By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The booming rollout of artificial intelligence technology could strain the US economy’s capacity and further boost inflation that the Federal Reserve will have to counteract, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said on Thursday, as AI firm Anthropic set a new record for an initial public offering of stock. "The AI boom is contributing to the potential of overheating in the economy. I find it hard to ... look at that any other way," Goolsbee said in a conference call with reporters. "When you’re getting major business investment, almost unprecedented levels of business investment, there’s a high danger that the economy’s capacity cannot handle that kind of a pig through the python." Goolsbee said he sees the multitrillion-dollar pipeline of data-center projects already adding to what he referred to as "borderline, disturbingly high inflation rates" that are well above the Fed’s 2% target and potentially heading higher. He said he felt the Anthropic IPO, giving the company’s early shareholders the ability to tap equity holdings well in excess of $1 trillion, could on its own become relevant to the path of the broader economy. ... In the meantime, the Fed will have to cope with short-term effects that so far seem to be inflationary. "The Fed’s job is to prevent this thing from overheating the economy," with monetary policy set tight enough to keep demand and supply in balance, Goolsbee said at the event. The Chicago Fed chief did not say if he would support a larger half-percentage-point rate hike at the December meeting, as at least one of his colleagues has advocated, but added that all options were on the table. "The question of how steep the rate path is going to be and if there will be any rate increases should be determined, in my view, by whether you think inflation is going to be heading back to 2% on its own or not," Goolsbee said. "The evidence does not suggest we’re on a path back to 2%."

items.title: Fed’s Jefferson says AI boosting inflation, productivity impact possible ’in the future’ By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The rapid artificial intelligence buildout is putting upward pressure on US inflation through its impact on demand, Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said on Thursday, with possible productivity gains that could help ease price pressures only coming "in the future." In prepared remarks to a Brazilian central bank conference, Jefferson said the AI boom is the sort of shock that could influence both demand and supply, but at different points in time. "On the demand side, optimism about the technology has been boosting business investment in data centers, advanced computing equipment, and related products," Jefferson said. "Currently, the AI buildout is exerting upward pressure on demand and inflation." Productivity improvements from the new technology could put downward pressure on prices, but only "in the future," Jefferson said, without estimating a timeline.

Speaking to TIME magazine as part of its TIME100 Next India feature, Alia Bhatt addressed the online discussions about her marriage to Ranbir Kapoor and the claims that she is in an ‘unequal marriage’. Alia also suggested that the speculation could stem from the fact that her relationship does not follow conventional ideas of marriage.
